name: Hipcooks
bio: Learn, Cook, EAT, & have fun! Hands-on cooking classes that end as a meal with new friends. We offer individual and group classes, as well as gift certificates. Patrick Haemmerlein- Immersed in a layered urban paradigm of reality versus fantasy, Patrick Haemmerlein creates a visual soundtrack as a backdrop to his stark silhouettes, choreographing torn pages of poetry and bars of music from the 1800’s and early 1900’s. Splashes of water color’s punctuate the delicate balance between urban sprawl and rural wildlife in Los Angeles. Haemmerlein begins his journey by taking countless photos of his environment exploring both urban and rural perspectives. He then manipulates the photographs, layering the images on wood until he is able to recreate the feeling of that moment and place. Using Los Angeles as his creative playground, his recycled articles often include sheet music, books he has found and paint. The result is a timeless tangible sonnet to the city he loves, and his thirst to rediscover it endlessly. Lucia Reti- I am an artist with fire. (literally, look at my head) In my art, I try to bring to life the unnoticed things in the everyday world. In the photos I take, I try to bring out different elements in what I see by experimenting with abstract backgrounds, realistic focuses, color, and different mediums. I usually use whatever I have around, because when I get the urge to make art, I just grab supplies as quickly as I can and create (with my adhd, I have to take what I can get with my spontaneous bursts of energy). I mostly use acrylic paint, oil pastels, and random drawing materials such as pens or pencils. Making my art is draining and regenerating all at once. It’s somewhere to put my emotions while releasing them, something to make out of it. At 16, I’m trying to make my way in the art world, fighting back on stupid stereotypes, making something physical and beautiful, something real, trying to capture the beauty and the rawness of life.

name: Matt Ullman
bio: ARTIST STATEMENT: Graduating from Webster University with a degree in Film & Video Production in 1989, I followed my fellow St. Louis filmmaking friends out to Hollywood. After 20 years of working in The Business, mostly as an in-house photographer/videographer/archivist at make-up special effects shops, I started to expand my creative horizons, and began experimenting with casting cement forms around 2010. With an affinity for functional art, I found a purpose for these creations by adapting my designs into candle holders, clocks, planters, containers, and incense burners. A chance encounter with square candles inspired my “Frank Lloyd Wright meets Ancient Mayan Ruin meets Sci-Fi” style. My love of Brutalist Architecture is also a major influence. Being invited to participate in Chet Zar’s annual Conjoined art show has inspired me to up my game, and I find myself leaning more towards creating fine art pieces, now.

name: Teale Hatheway
bio: Teale Hatheway Fine Artist – TealeHatheway.com – Architectural Paintings Founder | Creative Director – PearlandMaude.com – Home Décor Design Studio Co-Founder – StripedWallpaper.com – For Rebels with a Ruler Teale Hatheway is a Los Angeles-based artist known for her paintings and installations exploring architecture, streetlights, and ornamental detail. Her work contemplates memory, time, and the soulful residue left behind as people move through physical spaces. Teale’s paintings are held in over 200 public, private, and corporate collections. Her entrepreneurial spirit extends to two home décor lines specializing in high-end wallcoverings. Studio Location: 1918 N Main Street #101 Los Angeles, CA 90031

name: Theory Labs
bio: Theory Labs is home to some of the most talented artists at the Brewery and a gathering spot for the artist community for over twenty years. Kalon Fowler’s works are a whimsical and colorful exploration of the world through his idiosyncratic lens.

name: Napkin Killa
bio: Get your face drawn on a napkin by the world’s most famous (napkin) artist, Napkin Killa, at the brand new Killa Lounge. This LA native was reborn as the Cartoon Assassin in a Brooklyn dive bar, as he doodled unsuspecting victims on cocktail napkins. Though this all started as a goof, it accidentally became a career. For the past decade, Napkin Killa has drawn portraits at corporate, celebrity & private events worldwide. Nap doesn’t just serve on serviettes. He creates on all mediums, from murals to clothing. Nap also has a cartoon dog you can meet named NapDog, a half asleep, half awake pitbull who guards our collective subconscious. See you at the Killa Lounge!

name: Claudia Endler Designs
bio: http://claudiaendler.com Claudia Endler Designs creates contemporary jewelry that fuses graphic design, art, and architecture. Each piece embodies architectural and geometric elegance, sculpted to evoke both movement and substance. “As an artist, I’ve always sought to illuminate the unseen — to give form to experience. My journey into modern jewelry has reflected my own path of self-discovery and empowerment. Minimalist design, with its clarity and focus, reveals the essence of each element and mirrors my embrace of purpose and truth. As this exploration deepened, I discovered the joy of sharing it with my clients — transforming creation into a shared experience of meaning, collaboration, and magic.”

name: Nicola Collection
bio: Nicola Collection proudly presents an upcoming gallery exhibition celebrating the evolving voices of emerging and mid-career artists. This thoughtfully curated show brings together a dynamic range of perspectives across contemporary art. A featured portion of the exhibition highlights the timeless and transformative theme of florals, expressed through photography, painting, and collage. Alongside this, the broader collection showcases a diverse selection of abstract works, offering bold explorations of form, color, and emotion. Join us as we showcase a diverse collection that honors both artistic development and creative exploration. Our group show includes art from Nicola Katsikis, Annie Rob, Bloomer aka Nicholas Sitter, Bryn Williams, My Strange Honey, Tanner Goldbeck and Amy Smith.

name: Shoebox Arts / Kristine Schomaker
bio: Kristine Schomaker KRISTINE’S SWEET SHOPPE OF LIBERATION Step right up to the most unusual candy store you’ve ever encountered! Behind the vintage charm and sweet facade of Kristine’s Sweet Shoppe of Liberation lies 52 years of carefully curated chaos – shredded, sorted, and packaged for your revolutionary pleasure. What’s on the shelves? Delightful 3x3x3 acrylic cubes filled with “liberation blends” – shredded CD inserts from a collection lost 15 years ago, painted Yogurtland spoons from an eating disorder recovery journey, fragments of cut-up wigs, transparencies, and documents that no longer serve their original purpose. Each cube is a tiny time capsule of transformation, a confection of controlled destruction. The walls themselves become part of the installation – a POW of pattern and color that turns the space into a virtual candy store where memory, identity, and letting go are the main ingredients. This isn’t your grandmother’s sweet shop (though she’d recognize the aesthetic). This is where Fluxus meets confectionery, where Piero Manzoni’s spirit runs the register, and where buying a $20 cube makes you a collaborator in radical liberation. Each purchase doesn’t just sweeten your collection – it actively participates in dismantling barriers, taking up space, and proving that what we destroy can become more precious than what we keep. Come for the nostalgia. Stay for the revolution. Leave with a piece of freedom you can hold in your hands. 10% of proceeds benefit eating disorder recovery www.kristineschomaker.net @kristineschomaker Shoebox Arts Let Me Eat Cake, Please! Warning: This exhibition may cause sudden cravings for dessert and an uncontrollable urge to lick gallery walls. “Let Me Eat Cake, Please!” serves up 80+ food-focused artworks that transform Shoebox into a confectionery fever dream. Every surface is covered salon-style with chocolate drips, abstract candy explosions, and birthday cake nostalgia that hits harder than your third espresso. What started as curator Kristine Schomaker’s obsession with Baroque excess has evolved into something tastier – a space where art creates conversations about comfort, memory, and our deliciously complicated relationships with food. Working through her own experience with disordered eating, Schomaker has curated a show that understands sweetness as both pleasure and politics, that dessert can be rebellion. Come hungry. Leave satisfied. And maybe with chocolate paintings you can’t actually eat but definitely want to own. A portion of proceeds benefits the National Alliance for Eating Disorders. Online store live at https://www.shoeboxarts.com/ category/all-products – because the best art makes you want seconds. @ shoeboxarts.la

name: The I5 Gallery
bio: Kate McCallum An innovative arts and multi-media development and production company presenting THE ART OF SOUND art+music boutique label and gallery Kate McCallum’s introduction to the arts was through her training as a flutist and an operatic soprano. She studied music, creative theory, communications and media arts at Western Michigan University and received a BA In Communications with a Minor in Music. Kate also studied photography at the Kalamazoo Institute of Art. She relocated from Michigan to Los Angeles and found her way into the entertainment industry. Working first on several music videos for MTV in a variety of positions, and as Script Supervisor for an independent feature starring Tony Curtis and Dee Wallace Stone, Kate discovered her calling as a creative producer and writer. Kate spent 20 years working at NBCUniversal and Paramount Studios in the development and production of primetime scripted television, long-form and feature films working alongside some of the top writers and showrunners in the industry, and for eight of those years she served as a creative development executive. While honing her professional skills and a deep understanding of story, Kate kept her own personal art spirit alive by opening a photography studio, and writing spec scripts and TV series concepts while working days in the studios. Kate loves collaborating with other creatives and artists and founded Bridge Arts Media, LLC in 2004 so that she could work in a variety of mediums including film, photography, live events, books, and magazines. Because of her love for music, she launched a unique music+art label called THE ART OF SOUND bringing together visual artists and musicians to create not just albums, but live performances, artwork and eventually fulldome immersive and VR content which is what she is producing today. Her first fulldome art+music concert took place in The Vortex Dome with visual artist Audri Phillips and musician/composer, Winter Lazerus. She then went on to produce several more fulldome music+art concerts, and she produced the award-winning 360 fulldome shows Mesmerica and Beautifica with James Hood and director Michael Saul. Kate is also collaborated on an award-winning fulldome show, The Journey 360, with musicians Jahna and Michael Perricone; animator and director, Brianna Amore; and executive producer, Ed Lantz. Currently, she is completing Astronomica , the third dome show with musician James Hood and director, Michael Saul for www.changeworlds.org . In 2019, she collaborated with artist and performer Elizabeth Yochim to produce the short film Angelbird , performed as a vocalist with Elizabeth in a performance art piece and film called Essence which was featured at the Fine Arts Building during Artwalk Los Angeles, and she also performed with Elizabeth at the Los Angeles Union Station. Kate holds an MA in Consciousness Studies and has been passionate about human potential, spirituality, new media tech and future studies, and in 2004, she co-founded the c3: Center for Conscious Creativity www.consciouscreativity.org 501(c3) with former Brewery tenant Philip Horvath. Together, they hosted several events at the Brewery along with residents Barry Goldberg and Stosh www.theartofsoundgallery.com www.bridgeartsmedia.com

name: Atelier Francine Lecoultre
medium: Fabric Collection, Sculptural Objects, 3D Printing, Painting
bio: Atelier Francine www.atelierfrancine.art Francine Lecoultre is an artist, designer and artisan. She has a passion for innovation and Science-Fiction, with cutting-edge technology, combining research and history. Francine has worked on numerous Hollywood movies and theatrical productions around the world, designing costumes and creating unique specialty fabrics for iconic fantastical characters. Working in her Studio at The Brewery Art Community, Francine favors complex techniques built in superposition, such as sculpting, molding, silk screening, and more recently 3D printing combined with metal plating. Her theatrical art installations, costume concepts, and otherworldly creations are telling unique stories with aliens, mutants and different species from other galaxies in a distant future.

name: Flor Quinto
bio: Flor Quinto describes her process as a conversation with mystery. Her sculptural paintings include used objects, discarded from her own life or that of a loved one . Her compositions come together in the moment, guided by the play between materials. Wax and resin flow between shattered glass . Warped cassette tape becomes drawing. Capsules explode under the heat gun. Eye shadow crumbles, a new texture is born.Through this practice of salvage and transformation, Flor is e xplori ng her complicated relationship with change. Every finished piece is part personal archaeology , p art celebration of the profound stories embedded in our most overlooked possessions. Each piece asks: What do we keep? What do we release? And what happens in that space between holding on and letting go? my website: https://florquinto. com/ contact info:

name: Guillermo Bert's Studio
bio: Los Angeles-based multi-media artist Guillermo Bert was born in Santiago, Chile in 1959. His bi-cultural experience provides him with a lived perspective from which his artistic expression is cultivated. Bert combines his decades-long practice of working with cultural symbols of urbanism, consumerism, and displacement – dating back to his 1990s iterations of street-level ‘bricolage’ that delved into the urban archaeology of street posters along Los Angeles’s skid row. From there, he modified his commodities work to incorporate electronic barcodes into laser cuts and paintings, until his first trip home to Chile in 2010. That trip marked a turning point in his work through his experience collaborating with the indigenous Mapuche community’s traditional weavers. He worked with the weavers to integrate functional QR codes into traditional textile designs. These “high tech” QR codes, when scanned with a smartphone, take the viewer into a filmic world of story, myth, and reflection by Mapuche elders, activists, and poets. Extending this idea, Bert continues to experiment with this multi-layered format, collaborating to date with Mapuche, Navajo, Maya, Mixtec, and Zapotec weavers. The result is a series of 40 embedded films that “decode” cultural messaging and create a bond between the distant viewer and the intimacy of the community of indigenous artists and storytellers. The filmic and multimedia aspects of the project, while intrinsic to the textile project as a whole, also stand alone as visual media testimony and glimpses into cultural life through documentary inquiry and observation. In his video production work of the last five years, Bert has trained the camera on the urgency of the messages relayed and traveled through the artworks of indigenous artists. The artists in these films speak for themselves, often in the voices of their indigenous languages. These 40 short films from more than 7 countries, approximately 10 minutes each, will be woven together to form a “mini-series”. The project continues to unfold, including all manner of content and forms along the media spectra – from weavings to laser sculptures to photographs to film. Bert’s work will be featured in a major mid-career retrospective at the Nevada Museum of Art in autumn 2023, accompanied by a 200+ page catalog. His work was recently acquired by The Smithsonian’s Renwick Gallery and will be included in their 50th-anniversary exhibition “Crafting a New World” opening in May 2022. LACMA and the Rhode Island Museum of Art also recently bought pieces for their permanent collections. Bert has exhibited his work nationally and internationally at museums and galleries including Queens Museum in NY, Palm Springs Museum, Lille3000 in France, Anchorage Museum in Alaska, Nevada Museum of Art, MoLAA (Museum of Latin American Art), Pasadena Museum of California Art, Museum of Art and Design in New York, shows with L.A./L.A. Pacific Standard Time and the Folk and Craft Museum, and UCR (Riverside) His work has been reviewed nationally and internationally by Smithsonian Magazine, ArtNews Magazine, LA Times and LA Weekly. He was awarded a COLA individual artist grant from the City of Los Angeles Cultural Affairs Department, received the California Community Foundation Fellowship in 2015, the Center for Cultural Innovation Quick Grant for Education in 2015, and the 2010 Master Artist Grant from the National Association of Latino Arts. Bert’s career as an artist and educator takes many forms including Art Director for the Los Angeles Times (1995-2000) and Professor of Mixed Media at the Art Center School of Design, Pasadena, California. During the pandemic, Bert participated in several online talks with museums including The Museum of Art and Design in NY, The George Washington University Museum in DC, and The Long Beach Museum of Latin American Art.

name: Nicole Fournier
bio: http://www.nicolefournier.com Nicole Fournier first discovered her passion for photography during a fourth-grade class trip to Washington D.C. when she slipped away to take a picture of a spiral staircase. This fascination became a path followed, in obtaining a BFA graduating cum laude, and growing into a professional career in fine arts and photography. Her art today is a combination of photography and encaustic, transferring images she has photographed directly into an encaustic (wax) medium, then embellishing them with colored wax mediums combined from oil-based or powder pigments. Encaustic painting is one of the oldest forms of art known to man, and examples can be found from as far back as the Egyptian Fayum Mummy portraits over 2,500 years ago. These paintings are resistant to moisture, acid, and mold, and thus contain excellent archival properties. Nicole enjoys the wide range of possibilities inherent in this technique; the evocative and distressed tones, and especially the additive and subtractive qualities that come along with the process. Through her work, she continues to express concepts of growth and awareness, and to promote the preservation of our external environment, along with the cultivation of our inner self. Nicole Fournier is located at the Brewery Arts Complex in Los Angeles, California. She has been participating in their biannual open studio events since 2007, and she also teaches encaustic workshops held there in her studio. She can be reached at Nicole.Doris.Fournier@gmail.com .

name: Sandy Shimooka
bio: I like creating scavenger hunts that prompt people to ask questions and inspire them to want to learn more. My work uses storytelling that weaves history, art, art history and culture into interactive, community engagement installations. I want to highlight the commonalities that tie the past to the present. The installations are designed to engage viewers on many levels, using a mixture of figurative, conceptual and abstract motifs. Most elements can stand on their own as art centerpieces. They are designed to allow a range of audiences to interact with the story in non-linear ways. I hope that artful exchange might inspire thinking about our common origins and our shared futures. My art usually combines collage, sculpture, painting, video, photography and sound. Installations also often incorporate research, books, writing, ephemera and archival materials. Interview/article link: https://voyagela.com/ interview/check-out-sandy- shimookas-story

name: Susan Savory
bio: Susan Savory was born and raised in a small city on the banks of the Susquehanna River in Central New York. After completing her BFA in Illustration at Parsons School of Design in New York City, she worked as an illustrator, with a special affection for children’s picture books. Susan has experimented in almost every medium: painting and drawing as well as glass, clay, fiber and metal, and has shown her work in galleries and museums throughout New York, New England and California. She has curated several gallery shows in Maine, Massachusetts, and Los Angeles; and was the curator/manager of the Art, Craft & Design Showcase for the League of New Hampshire Craftsmen from 2016 through 2023. Her most recent personal works include a series of mixed media assemblages built with vintage photographs, found objects, oil pastel and colored pencil. Susan also creates jewelry incorporating her own metalwork and lampwork glass beads as well as antique silver, stones, and other small treasures collected in her extensive travels. Savory has been a Brewery (and California) resident since January of 2014. www.susansavory.com instagram – @spiritboxinsocal facebook – Susan Savory Dean

name: Stephanie Vosper
bio: Stephanie Vosper is a self-taught artist. She created McDisco, an installation made of inflatable dolls for New Zealand’s Regional Burning Man festival Kiwiburn in 2016. Stephanie sources inspiration from everywhere and anywhere, hence great variety in her work and interests, which range from trophy sculptures to paintings, crystal mandalas and flowers, interiors, indoor fountains, 3D and beyond. megatrophywife.com

name: Bruce Dean
bio: After receiving his MFA from Otis Art Institute in 1974, Bruce Dean began his career as an illustrator. His work was featured in scores of national and international publications and received numerous awards, including a silver medal from the Society of Illustrators of Los Angeles. After a decade, Bruce had his first solo show of abstractions at the Karl Bornstein Gallery in Santa Monica, CA. He has since participated in over forty gallery and museum exhibitions nation-wide. His work includes projects funded by grants from the Department of Education and the Foundation for Global Community Bruce Has taught a variety of art classes at C.S,U.N., Mt. St. Mary’s College, and Otis College of Art and Design. He recently taught drawing seminars at the Museum of African American Art, and life drawing seminars to University of Southern California medical students. He was the featured artist in the December, 2018 issue of Voyage LA magazine. Bruce was interviewed about his newest work in an article titled, “Memories, Mystery and Truth,” in Create! Magazine. Bruce’s studio is one of four featured in the film, “The Brewery. Art Lives Here.” Artist Statement: Each new series begins intuitively, with a focus on exploring unfamiliar territory. Over time, the narrative becomes clear. My work is about communication. I am trying to access imagery and an essential aesthetic that I believe I share with all humans, perhaps at some pre-language level. My newest work is about the path without a clear destination, the journey one takes without an understanding of what is being sought, the dream whose details have receded, the memory that is fading around the edges, The work is meant to convey that there is something of importance, some question answered, but the answers remain just out of reach. Bruce’s email Bruce’s website Bruce’s fine art prints on etsy Bruce on instagram Bruce on facebook

name: Christopher Ulrich
bio: Christopher Ulrich is a painter of surreal iconographic images. He is influenced by the richness of ancient mythology, the mystery of alchemy, and the vastness of cosmic reality. Illuminating this dark journey with insight, heart and determination he strives to understand the unraveling revelation that reveals itself in the work. Since the commencement of the Demoneater Saga, Christopher has participated in-group exhibitions at L.A.C.M.A., The William Roland Gallery of Fine Arts, L.A. Art Show, Century Guild, Copro Gallery, BASH Contemporary Gallery, Michael Kate Interiors & Art Gallery, Mesa Contemporary Arts Museum, Grand Central Art Center, Rete Museale of Cosenza, Mondo POP International Gallery of Italy, Gallery 1988, Corey Helford and Torrance Art Museum. Ulrich painted large murals, made masks, banners and shields for Old Town Pasadena’s bier Haus DerWolfskopf and Rathskeller. Currently, in addition to painting, Ulrich has the pleasure of collaborating with Blitzkrieg Toys and Creature Bizarre. He is also working on storyboarding several collaborative projects at this time. Email: ulrichart@gmail.com Website: www.christopherulrich.com Artist page: @artistchristopherulrich Toy collaborator pages: @blitzkriegtoys, @creature_bazaar

name: Emily Halpern
medium: Large Paintings & Small Works on Paper
bio: Emily Elisa Halpern was raised in Canada and studied Criminology and was a professional athlete in Europe and Australia before changing courses and studying art. She received a BFA at New York’s Pratt Institute and an MFA at San Diego State University. Her work has won her several scholarships and awards. Halpern’s paintings operate between symbol and metaphor. They map an inner world and a complex emotional landscape. Her work is a diary of fragments from dreams, incidents from daily life, and internal monologues that ground the work in a personal mythology. Strong emotional undercurrents combine with murky narratives of danger, loss and destruction, reflecting a sense of unease in an unpredictable world. She draws from her life experiences, relationships, current events and the processes inspired by Jung and the Surrealists that seek to unlock the door of the unconscious. She aspires to create work that deepens our understanding of the ways in which certain personal meanings reflect the complex matrix of universally shared emotions.

name: Gabe Leonard
bio: Gabe Leonard is an American Artist Gabe Leonard’s artistic journey and vision are deeply intertwined with his personal experiences, challenges, and growth as an artist. Each key element reflects specific moments and decisions in his life that have shaped his work and the stories he tells through art. By embracing authenticity, narrative depth, and a commitment to continuous improvement, Gabe has carved out a unique and impactful space in the art world. Drawing on the history and atmosphere of film, Gabe’s art features narratives from his own experiences and cultural history. His dedication to storytelling is what engages with viewers, bringing them in as participants to connect with the characters and scenes depicted in his paintings. It’s finding our reflection with the broader emotionally charged human perspective Gabe Leonard’s passion for storytelling is a driving force behind his artistic vision. That vision is expressed with a playful, spontaneous approach that aims to evoke the way it feels to be in this world. Gabe is also currently on an extensive, ongoing experimentation and study of both materials and techniques. Gabe draws the world around him in sketchbooks. Working primarily in oil, he experiments with color palettes, substrates and different types of mediums such as acrylic and watercolors. The constant deliberate study is where Gabe finds new ways to express new ideas to the best of his ability. IG @gabeleonardart

name: Jane the Artist
bio: Samantha Jane Harrold paints her emotions, disguised as portraits of whimsical children, with exaggerated details. She paints herself, over and over again, to release all the wild parts of her, into the world. She signs her work with “Jane,” her middle name, inherited by her great grandmother who was also an artist. instagram @signedjanetheartist venmo @signedJanetheartist Email signedjanetheartist@gmail.com When she isn’t painting her own feelings, she helps others discover they have no bad parts by offering trauma conscious somatic therapy and clinical art therapy through her telehealth only private practice Moth & Flame ( mothandflametherapy.com and instagram @mothandflame_therapy). Jane graduated from UCSB with a BA in Psychology and Art in 2013, and Loyola Marymount University in 2025 with an MA in Clinical Art Therapy and Marriage and Family Therapy. She has been painting since she was a child, has been working as an Board Certified Art Therapist since 2015. Currently showing work at The Hive Gallery in downtown LA and participating in both fall and spring LA Brewery Art Walks. Jane identifies as a witch of many crafts, and though her favorite medium is oil painting, she also designs and sews her own clothes, sculpts clay dolls and uses a variety of art materials and word craft. Each painting births its own poem and she writes fiction in her space time. “I shall wear midnight” “Who’s afraid of the big bad wolf? (Not me)” “The forest” “The light” “Spring witch” All pieces are 16×20 in water mixable oils on wood panels -Samantha JANE Harrold LMFT, ATR-BC

name: Jill Sykes
bio: We as artists create objects that nourish and enrich existence, and as such what we do, consciously or not, has profound effect. The images I create are about life and the sheltering aspects of Nature – I focus on botanical forms and the abstracted spaces I find between individual branches and leaves. These paintings are sophisticated in terms of color and form, and yet remain incredibly soothing and serene to look at. Jill Sykes is a painter living in Los Angeles. Her work is included in many private and corporate collections including Omgivning Architecture Interiors, Kelly Wearstler, Kovac Design Studios, Saks Fifth Avenue as well as many others. Her paintings have been featured in exhibitions throughout Southern California and across the country including The Sturt Haaga Gallery at Descanso Gardens in La Canada Flintridge, CA., The Museum of Art + History (MOAH) in Lancaster, CA, the Santa Paula Art Museum in Santa Paula, CA, El Camino College Art Gallery in Torrance, CA, and Tobey C. Moss Gallery in Los Angeles, CA. Jill and fellow Brewery artist Ada Pullini Brown were co-curators of the 2022 exhibition, Let Me Talk , at the Brand Library and Art Center in Glendale, CA. www.jillsykes.com 696 Moulton Avenue #A

name: Joshua Elias
medium: Oil on Canvas / Oil on Linen
bio: ARTIST STATEMENT My work explores the layered terrain of memory, personal history, and the ephemeral nature of time. Each painting acts as both a map and a meditation — a visual record of inner landscapes shaped by experience, spiritual inquiry, and the unseen vibrations that connect us all. Working in large-scale abstraction, I begin with constraints — limited palettes, specific materials — then allow spontaneity, intuition, and chance to guide my process. The resulting works are both containers and portals: structured yet expansive, rooted yet transcendent. Poetry and language quietly inform my practice. Though no text appears in the work itself, the rhythm of words, the shape of silence, and the tension between presence and absence all find their way into the paint. Joshua Elias 2025 Studio- 600 Moulton Avenue #204 http://www.joshuaelias.com

name: Sullivan Clare Williams
bio: Sullivan Clare Williams’ work captures the elusive feelings of dreams and non verbal experience. Playing in surrealist landscapes with hyper-realistic subjects, Williams’ work analyzes the purpose of selfhood through an internal lens with a dash of punk actualization. Their visual vocabulary reveals moments of brevity by use of figures in moments of realization. They are a mixed media artist with a primary focus in acrylic portraiture as well as figurative and abstract sculpture. Williams’ work embodies the vulnerability of unseen moments as well as the Intimacy of solitude and self reflection. Bio: Williams (b. 2000) was raised in Los Angeles, California and received their BFA in the inaugural graduating class of Collaborative Arts at New York University in 2023. Since graduating, they have been an artistic fellow at The Newington-Cropsey Foundation, studying as an apprentice under renowned sculptor, Greg Wyatt. Exhibitions include: Spotlight on Art, Fine Arts Federation Annual Show,Betsey Lueke Gallery, Los Angeles (2026); Brewery Art Walk , Los Angeles (2025); Fine Arts Federation Annual Show , Betsey Lueke Gallery, Los Angeles (2025); Artist in Residence Showcase, Burren College of Art, Co. Clare, Ireland (2024); Female Art Night , Sab Gallery Collection, Los Angeles (2024). They have been an Artist in Residence at the Burren College of Art in County Clare, Ireland (2024), as well as Azule in North Carolina for painting (2024). Currently, they live and work in Los Angeles.

name: Todd Westover
bio: As a child, Todd began doodling the Flower-Power graphics popular in the 1960s and 70s. With the deft utilization of simple forms, he is able to create portraits, houses, scenics, full-figure nudes, abstract statements and vases on tables. The repetitive rounded curves and flowing circles have a familiar sensuality that most people, consciously or not, seem to find appealing and comforting. His paintings and murals all share the same joyous iconographic doodles of his youth, thereby fulfilling his desire to bring a smile to your face, and a bit more joy into the world. His paintings are a celebration of life, as flowers are a symbol of renewal and regrowth. The message: Enjoy life. Todd is currently a resident of the famous Brewery Arts Colony in Los Angeles, CA. westovertodd.com Social media: Instagram: @westovertodd Facebook: todd.westover.104 website: westovertodd.com 2100 N Main st #B14

name: Panda Roja Design
bio: ARTIST STATEMENT: Luminous Echoes of the Lived Experience is a light-based installation that explores the cyclical nature of human emotion. The installation features a series of eight light portraits that use light, reflection, and refraction to depict a distinct inner state—from the bright spontaneity of Joy to the stillness of Silence. This is not a linear story of a lifetime, but rather a universal arc of experience that repeats throughout our lives: a moment of searching, a period of turmoil, a quiet descent into sadness, and a hard-won moment of resilience. These light portraits invite the viewer to witness the intangible by using light to give shape to the emotions we feel, analyze, and learn from over and over again. Panda Roja Design, 620 Moulton Ave #104

name: Wild Don Lewis
bio: Wild Don Lewis graduated with a BFA in photography and painting from Cornell University. He then moved to LA, where he documented the punk scene of the 80s, and the indie scene of the 90s-2000s. He is currently documenting the exploding noise scene. He has shot for the LA Weekly, Rolling Stone, and New Times Los Angeles, among others, and created album covers for the Melvins (Atlantic Records), Jawbreaker (Geffen), and bands on SST Records. email: info@wilddonlewis.com phone/text: 323-742-6904 Instagram: @wilddonlewis Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/wilddonlewis website: https://wilddonlewis.photoshelter.com Studio Address: 2020 N Main St. Unit 014, Los Angeles CA 90031

name: Jane Szabo Photography
bio: Los Angeles-based conceptual artist Jane Szabo merges a love for fabrication and materials with visceral photographic images. The core of her work revolves around ideas; she uses photography as a storytelling medium, where the narratives are deeply rooted in personal experiences. Her images can be seen as a diary that records details of life over time, or a series of self-portraits, even when she is not physically present in them. Szabo’s work has been exhibited in solo shows at institutions such as the Forsberg Gallery at Lower Columbia College, Huntley Gallery at Cal Poly Pomona, Danforth Art Museum, Griffin Museum of Photography, Koslov Larsen Gallery, John Wayne Orange County Airport, Museum of Art & History in Lancaster, CA, Foto Museum Casa Coyoacán in Mexico City, Orange County Center for Contemporary Art, Yuma Fine Art Center Arizona, and the Los Angeles Center for Digital Art. Among many other locations, her work has been included in group exhibitions at Spartanburg Art Museum, Oceanside Museum of Art, Florida Museum of Photographic Arts, The Brand Library Gallery, Colorado Center for Photographic Arts, Photo LA, LA Art Fair, San Diego Art Institute, Los Angeles Center for Photography, Kaohsiung International Photographer Exhibition in Taiwan, and Foto Fever in Paris, France. Szabo’s art is in the permanent collections of Los Angeles County Museum of Art, Museum of Art & History, Arte al Limite Santiago, Chile, Centro de Arte Faro Cabo Mayor in Santander, Spain and in private collections throughout the U.S. and Europe. She holds an MFA from Art Center College of Design in Pasadena, CA. www.janeszabophotography.com Instagram @JaneSzaboPhoto 2100 N. Main, #B-10

name: Marcia Mesquita-Payne
bio: Marcia Mesquita 2100 N Main St #A3 Los Angeles CA 90031 Born in Brazil, Marcia lived in São Paulo until moving to Europe. She lived in Portugal and Italy for several years and now resides in Los Angeles, California. She has loved literature since she learned to read; and has been enchanted by words and their meanings; making books her passion and, later, a passion for human society and its customs, its countries, and its cities. Although it took years to leave her native country, she knew there were horizons on land and oceans. She studied law. Criminal law was her goal. Nearing the end of her degree, now familiar with the laws and their loopholes—more loopholes than laws—she gave up her journey because she knew it was impossible to bring justice to the dead, her clients. She left her homeland and traveled… Taking some books and notebooks with her, (she couldn't take her whole library), she continued to read, write, and record her daily observations and everything she encountered along the way. Over time, she realized she couldn't walk the streets with a diary jotting down everything she saw, and that she couldn’t store it all reliably as memories. She bought a camera, knowing it would provide a colorful record that would mark her path to survival in the face of loneliness, existential emptiness, and the search for meaning in life.

name: Richard Wilks
bio: A Los Angeles-based artist, designer, and creative engineer, Richard Wilks received his BFA in 1988 from the Art Center College of Design in Pasadena. He began his career as an experiential designer for clients including Disney, Target, and Nokia, creating environments encouraging conversation and connection. Now, fusing the eclectic influences of commercial art, the maker movement, and festival culture, Wilks continually expands the scope and breadth of his dynamic sculptures and installations. He uses a combination of physical and digital tools to build pieces from steel, aluminum, and plastic waste, conceptualizing and crafting original machines and fabrication processes to bring his work to life. By drawing parallels between biological and mechanical processes, Wilks challenges the distinctions between natural and artificial, individual and environment. His artworks engage viewers in full-body experiences that prompt them to reconsider their relationships to objects, space, and one another. Each of Wilks’s sculptural pieces is motivated by a relentless curiosity about our essential humanity, and requires physical interaction to reach their full potential. Participants use their hands to send the Liquid Forest , a series of luminescent sculptures made from recycled plastic, spinning. Wilks’s inventive vehicles, the Aquatrope and Evotrope — inspired by our elemental connections to the natural world—are ready to drive. Organic shapes like circles and spirals are frequent motifs across Wilks’s work, mirroring Earth’s cycles and seasons. Likewise, Wilks’s fabrication processes often mimic biological ones, with his bespoke machines digesting and transforming refuse into raw materials.

name: Dylan Jones
bio: Dylan Jones Dylan Jones (b. 1998) is a painter, sculptor, and performance artist originally from the Bay Area. His art practice is a continuous world building project which hosts a growing lexicon of recurring characters, deities, and micro cultures. His most recent project involves a collection of game boards built by a group of beings called the Nylons, who feed on memories and look sort of like white blood cell teletubbies. When he is not making art, Dylan teaches Pilates at various studios throughout Los Angeles
